findings.description: The Lambda function embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key as plaintext environment variables directly in the Terraform configuration. These values are exposed in source control, in Terraform state, and to any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, and they bypass the function's own IAM execution role which already supplies temporary credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables are encrypted only with the AWS-managed default Lambda key. Any principal able to read the function configuration sees the decrypted values without needing a separate KMS grant, removing the second authorisation boundary that would otherwise protect the secret material stored there.

The function targets the nodejs12.x runtime, which is past end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS. Unpatched vulnerabilities accumulate in the runtime and its bundled dependencies such as OpenSSL and libc.
